items.definition: Kind, polite and generous to others.
items.sentence: The team stayed gracious in defeat and shook every opponent's hand.
items.hint: It comes from grace: drop the e and add -ious.

items.definition: Feeling that something is wrong or someone cannot be trusted.
items.sentence: The cat grew suspicious the moment the vet's carry cage appeared.
items.hint: Say sus-pi-cious, then finish with the -cious ending.

items.definition: Extremely hungry for something, such as food or books.
items.sentence: My little sister is a voracious reader who devours two novels weekly.
items.hint: It starts with vor-, from a root meaning to eat, then -acious.

items.definition: Wild, fierce and very strong.
items.sentence: A ferocious gust flipped our beach umbrella high over the dunes.
items.hint: The middle vowel is o, then the -cious ending.

items.definition: Deliberately mean and wanting to cause harm.
items.sentence: The story's malicious sorcerer was foiled by two quick-thinking sisters.
items.hint: The Latin root mal means bad; then add -icious.

items.definition: Made up; not real.
items.sentence: Every character in my story is fictitious, even the talking wombat.
items.hint: Fiction keeps its t, so the ending is -tious.

items.definition: Absolutely delicious to eat.
items.sentence: The tuckshop's scrumptious banana muffins vanish before the second bell.
items.hint: Remember the p after scrum, then the -tious ending.

items.definition: Changing suddenly and often, without any warning.
items.sentence: Spring weather here is capricious, sunny one minute and hailing the next.
items.hint: Say ca-pri-cious, ending with -cious, not -tious.

items.definition: To do with buying, selling and advertising.
items.sentence: Our media class filmed a funny commercial for imaginary sunscreen.
items.hint: Double m in the middle, then the -cial ending.

items.definition: Icy cold, or moving extremely slowly like a river of ice.
items.sentence: The queue for the water slide moved at a glacial pace.
items.hint: Start with glacier, drop the -er and add -al.

items.definition: Coming at the very beginning; first.
items.sentence: Our initial plan changed once we saw the storm forecast.
items.hint: After ini- comes the -tial ending, not -cial.

items.definition: Having the power to change what people think or do.
items.sentence: An influential coach convinced the council to build new netball courts.
items.hint: Build it from influence: drop the -ce and add -tial.

items.definition: Large in size, amount or importance.
items.sentence: The bake sale raised a substantial amount for the animal shelter.
items.hint: Think of substance, then swap the ending for -tial.

items.definition: To do with fighting skills or the armed forces.
items.sentence: Judo is a martial art that teaches balance, respect and control.
items.hint: It sounds like the name Marshall but is spelt with -tial.

items.definition: To do with the area where people live, or staying overnight somewhere.
items.sentence: Year seven is buzzing about the three-day residential camp in October.
items.hint: Build it from resident and add -ial.

items.definition: To do with a president or the job a president does.
items.sentence: Both candidates gave presidential speeches before the student council vote.
items.hint: Build it from president and add -ial.

items.definition: To show that you have noticed or accepted something.
items.sentence: Please acknowledge the umpire's decision with a nod and play on.
items.hint: Hide the whole word knowledge inside it, straight after ac-.

items.definition: Close to the exact amount, but not perfect.
items.sentence: Give an approximate distance from the surf club to the jetty.
items.hint: Double p near the start, just like approach.

items.definition: Easy to use or reach; causing no trouble.
items.sentence: The new drink fountain is convenient because it sits beside the courts.
items.hint: The tricky middle is -ven-, then -ient at the end.

items.definition: Polite behaviour and good manners.
items.sentence: Show some courtesy by holding the gate open for the riders.
items.hint: It begins like court and ends in -esy.

items.definition: Exactly right, with no mistakes.
items.sentence: Double-check your measurements so the model bridge is accurate.
items.hint: Double c near the start: ac-cu-rate.

items.definition: Showing huge interest and excitement.
items.sentence: The crowd gave an enthusiastic cheer when our band walked on stage.
items.hint: Start with enthusiasm, then swap the final m for -tic.

items.definition: A public display of artwork or interesting objects.
items.sentence: Our sculptures made from beach litter star in the school exhibition tonight.
items.hint: Remember the silent h straight after ex-.

items.definition: To retell just the main points in a shorter way.
items.sentence: Please summarise the chapter in three clear sentences.
items.hint: Double m in the middle, then the Australian -ise ending.

items.definition: The work of keeping something in good condition.
items.sentence: Regular maintenance keeps my bike chain quiet on the long ride home.
items.hint: Although it comes from maintain, the middle is -ten-, not -tain-.

items.definition: To tell the difference between things, or to stand out.
items.sentence: Can you distinguish a currawong's call from a magpie's carol?
items.hint: It ends in -guish, with u after the g.

items.definition: A mix of many different kinds of things.
items.sentence: The school fete offered a wonderful variety of stalls and games.
items.hint: Say var-i-e-ty so you remember the i before the e.

items.definition: To know someone or something because you have seen them before.
items.sentence: Did you recognise the mystery teacher in the old photo?
items.hint: Australian spelling uses the -ise ending, and never drop the g.

items.definition: The process of growing or getting better over time.
items.sentence: Coach tracks the development of every player across the season.
items.hint: Just add -ment to develop, with no extra e in between.

items.definition: The layer of air around the Earth, or the mood of a place.
items.sentence: The grand final's electric atmosphere gave everyone goosebumps.
items.hint: Greek roots: atmos means vapour and sphere means ball.

items.definition: A word that means the same, or nearly the same, as another word.
items.sentence: Find a strong synonym for said before you hand in your story.
items.hint: Syn- starts with s-y-n, and another y comes before the final m.

items.definition: A person who designs buildings.
items.sentence: An architect drew up the plans for our new library and stage.
items.hint: Greek origin: the ch makes a k sound, as in chaos.

items.definition: A comparison that uses like or as, such as brave as a lion.
items.sentence: Add a simile so readers can picture the roaring surf clearly.
items.hint: It looks like smile with an extra i: sim-i-le.

items.definition: The little star symbol used to mark something special in writing.
items.sentence: Put an asterisk beside any question you want to discuss tomorrow.
items.hint: From the Greek for little star; say the ending clearly: -risk.

items.definition: A wide, sweeping view of everything around you.
items.sentence: The lookout offers a stunning panorama of the valley and the ranges.
items.hint: Greek roots: pan means all and orama means view.

items.definition: The small punctuation mark that shows ownership or missing letters.
items.sentence: Remember the apostrophe when you write about your mum's famous pavlova.
items.hint: It ends in -phe, a Greek ending that sounds like fee.

items.definition: A careful scientific guess that you then test with experiments.
items.sentence: Our hypothesis was that seedlings near the window would grow fastest.
items.hint: Greek origin: hypo- starts with hy, then thesis follows.

items.definition: A long speech performed by one person.
items.sentence: For drama assessment, each student performs a two-minute monologue on stage.
items.hint: Mono means one, and the ending is -logue.

items.definition: A full list of items, such as books or products.
items.sentence: The library catalogue shows three copies of the new dragon novel.
items.hint: Australian spelling keeps the -logue ending, like monologue.

items.definition: A device that keeps the temperature steady by switching heating or cooling.
items.sentence: Dad tapped the thermostat because the lounge felt like a sauna.
items.hint: Thermo means heat and stat means staying steady.

items.definition: A large lake, often made by people, where water is stored.
items.sentence: Kayakers glided across the reservoir while we set up the tents.
items.hint: French origin: the ending -oir sounds like wah.

items.definition: A large waterproof sheet used for shelter or covering loads.
items.sentence: We strung a tarpaulin between the gums before the clouds burst.
items.hint: Three parts: tar-pau-lin, with au in the middle.

items.definition: Swimming face-down with a breathing tube to watch sea life.
items.sentence: We went snorkelling over the reef and counted eleven clownfish.
items.hint: Australian spelling doubles the l: snorkel plus -ling.

items.definition: An imagined situation and the way it might unfold.
items.sentence: Our debating coach gave each pair a tricky scenario to argue.
items.hint: Italian origin: sc makes an s sound, like in science.

items.definition: Done by choice, without being forced or paid.
items.sentence: Beach clean-ups are voluntary, yet half the school still turns up.
items.hint: Four syllables: vol-un-tar-y, with -ary at the end.

items.definition: A small, chatty Australian parrot often kept as a pet.
items.sentence: A wild budgerigar flock turned the outback sky bright green.
items.hint: Budgie is short for it: budg-er-i-gar.

items.definition: One part of something that comes in stages, like a story or payment.
items.sentence: The serial's final instalment airs on Friday after the news.
items.hint: Australian spelling uses one l: in-stal-ment.

items.definition: Meeting another line at a perfect right angle.
items.sentence: Draw one line perpendicular to the base of your triangle.
items.hint: Break it up: per-pen-dic-u-lar.

items.definition: A walkway between rows of seats or shelves.
items.sentence: We raced down the frozen-food aisle to grab icy poles for camp.
items.hint: It begins with a and hides a silent s: a-isle.

items.definition: Extremely funny.
items.sentence: The talent show's hilarious puppet act had teachers crying with laughter.
items.hint: One l only, then -arious: hi-lar-i-ous.

items.definition: Very curious and always asking questions.
items.sentence: Our inquisitive cockatiel opens the cage latch to explore the kitchen.
items.hint: Built from inquire: in-quis-i-tive.

items.definition: Able to float, or feeling cheerful and light.
items.sentence: Wetsuits keep you warm and slightly buoyant in the chilly surf.
items.hint: The u comes before the o, like in buoy.

items.definition: A planned series of actions to reach a goal.
items.sentence: Our recycling campaign halved the rubbish leaving the school canteen.
items.hint: A silent g hides in the -paign ending.

items.definition: Having two halves that match exactly.
items.sentence: Butterfly wings are perfectly symmetrical, like paint folded in half.
items.hint: Double m after sy: sym-met-rical.

items.definition: Complete confusion and disorder.
items.sentence: Feeding time caused happy chaos when the puppies spotted the biscuit tin.
items.hint: Greek origin: the k sound is spelt ch.

items.definition: A tall upright post, or a vertical strip of print in a newspaper.
items.sentence: Ivy climbed the old verandah column beside the fig tree.
items.hint: It ends with a silent n, like solemn.

items.definition: To honour and remember an important person or event.
items.sentence: A new mural will commemorate fifty years of our little surf club.
items.hint: Double m first, then single m: com-mem-orate.

items.definition: Letters, emails and other written messages between people.
items.sentence: Our class keeps up a lively correspondence with a school in Broome.
items.hint: Double r, then -ence at the end, not -ance.

items.definition: Going on and on without stopping.
items.sentence: The cicadas kept up a continuous hum all afternoon.
items.hint: After contin- comes -uous, with u-o-u-s at the end.

items.definition: Training yourself to work hard and follow the rules.
items.sentence: Daily discipline at training earned her a spot in the state squad.
items.hint: A quiet c follows the s: dis-ci-pline.

items.definition: Number eight in a line or order.
items.sentence: Our relay team came eighth, but we smashed our personal best.
items.hint: Write eight, then add one extra h at the end.

items.definition: The polite rules for how to behave in different situations.
items.sentence: Table etiquette at camp includes waiting until everyone is served.
items.hint: French origin: qu in the middle and double t near the end.

items.definition: Able to bounce back quickly after something difficult.
items.sentence: Saltbush is resilient, springing back even after the harshest summer.
items.hint: It ends in -ient: re-sil-i-ent.

items.definition: Great tiredness after hard work or exercise.
items.sentence: Despite her fatigue, the young hiker grinned at the summit cairn.
items.hint: French origin: the ending -gue sounds like a plain g.

items.definition: Famous and admired by many people.
items.sentence: The bakery is renowned for pies that sell out by nine.
items.hint: The middle rhymes with crown and is spelt the same way.

items.definition: A journey made by a group for a special purpose.
items.sentence: Our bushwalking expedition follows the river to the old fire tower.
items.hint: Say ex-pe-di-tion, with -dition like addition.

items.definition: A small square of cloth for wiping your nose or face.
items.sentence: Grandpa still keeps a folded handkerchief in his cardigan pocket.
items.hint: Hand plus kerchief, with a d you can barely hear.

items.definition: Active at night and asleep during the day.
items.sentence: Possums are nocturnal, so listen for them after the campfire dies.
items.hint: The Latin root noct means night: noc-tur-nal.

items.definition: A written plan of a journey listing places and times.
items.sentence: The camp itinerary promises canoeing, damper cooking and a night hike.
items.hint: Sound out all four parts: i-tin-er-ary.

items.definition: One of the first people to explore or start something new.
items.sentence: A local pioneer planted these fig trees more than a century ago.
items.hint: Three vowels in a row in the middle: pi-o-neer.

items.definition: A small flying insect that bites and leaves itchy lumps.
items.sentence: One whining mosquito kept the whole tent awake past midnight.
items.hint: Spanish origin: it ends in -quito, with qu for the k sound.

items.definition: A dish of beaten eggs cooked flat in a pan.
items.sentence: Dad flipped a fluffy cheese omelette for breakfast at the campsite.
items.hint: French origin: double t before the final silent e.

items.definition: A person travelling on foot.
items.sentence: New paths mean every pedestrian can cross the oval without muddy shoes.
items.hint: The Latin root ped means foot, as in pedal.

items.definition: Expecting good things to happen.
items.sentence: Despite the grey clouds, we stayed optimistic about the beach carnival.
items.hint: Build it from optimist and add -ic.

items.definition: So pretty it could belong in a painting or on a postcard.
items.sentence: We cycled through a picturesque village of stone cottages.
items.hint: Start with picture, then add the French-style ending -sque.

items.definition: Musical instruments you hit, shake or tap, like drums.
items.sentence: In percussion class we drummed rhythms on buckets and tapped triangles.
items.hint: Double s in the middle: per-cus-sion.

items.definition: A baked dish with flat pasta sheets layered with sauce.
items.sentence: Nonna's spinach lasagne disappears fastest at every family picnic.
items.hint: Australian spelling ends in -gne, from the Italian.

items.definition: An animal, like a frog, that lives both in water and on land.
items.sentence: The corroboree frog is a rare amphibian from the alpine bogs.
items.hint: The f sound in the middle is spelt ph: am-phib-ian.

items.definition: So important that you cannot manage without it.
items.sentence: A head torch is indispensable when the campsite lights go out.
items.hint: This one takes -able, even though sensible takes -ible.

items.definition: A full roll where your feet flip right over your head.
items.sentence: Lena nailed a somersault off the diving board at the carnival.
items.hint: It starts like summer but is spelt somer-, then -sault.
